item.title: Olympian accused of damaging Reflecting Pool seeks probe of potential misconduct
item.description: David Hearn is asking the Justice and Interior Dept. inspectors general to investigate his arrest and the dismissal of the case against him.

item.title: Trump suggests letting Iran "take out" LA, San Diego during rally
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom called President Trump "deranged and dangerous" after he suggested letting Iran "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego.

item.title: Amelia Earhart investigators to study mysterious object in Pacific
item.description: Investigators have begun an expedition to study a mysterious "visual anomaly" that they say may be Amelia Earhart's long-lost plane.

item.title: Cornell rape case provokes questions about ketamine use on campus
item.description: The prescription drug ketamine was referenced in the ongoing Cornell University rape case. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan to be executed by firing squad, Pentagon says
item.description: The Trump administration has approved a plan to execute former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan — who killed 13 people in a 2009 shooting at Fort Hood — by firing squad, the Pentagon said.

item.title: "NCIS: New York" stars LL Cool J and Scott Caan on what to expect this season
item.description: LL Cool J and Scott Caan join "CBS Mornings" to discuss "NCIS: New York," which premieres Tuesday night on CBS and Paramount+.

item.title: Fort Hood mass shooter could be executed by firing squad
item.description: Former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan killed 13 people in a 2009 shooting at Fort Hood. The Trump administration has approved a plan to execute Hasan by firing squad. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Iran's Houthi allies deny losing ground as Mideast crisis engulfs Yemen
item.description: Iran's Houthi allies deny losing ground to Yemen's Saudi-backed military, but oil prices ease despite the Middle East crisis erupting in a battle over control of another key waterway.

item.title: Tips on how to be liked from a behavorial researcher
item.description: Behavioral researcher Vanessa Van Edwards joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss her new book, "Conversation: How to Connect with Anyone & Make Every Interaction Count," which offers tips for anyone looking to improve their people skills.

item.title: Paramount closes $110 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery
item.description: The merger unites two major movie studios, news operations CBS News and CNN and cable networks including Comedy Central and TNT.

item.title: How beavers are protecting West London from flooding
item.description: Five Eurasian beavers were released into the town of Greenford in October 2023. Then, they got to work, felling trees, gathering branches and building dams.

item.title: Why you just got a $90 Social Security check — and who missed out
item.description: Millions of seniors are getting $90 direct deposits from Social Security this week, prompting questions about the source of the money.

item.title: Democrats see White House "pay for play" scheme with Balkan gas project
item.description: Democratic lawmakers accuse the Trump administration of lifting sanctions against a Bosnian Serb separatist leader in a bid to help enrich the president's allies.

item.title: Mexico arrests alleged cartel leader and fuel smuggler "The Tank"
item.description: Authorities say "El Tanque" runs a massive fuel theft network and is linked to homicides, kidnappings and drug trafficking.

item.title: Palestinian and Israeli activist duo join forces to urge peace, nearly 3 years after October 7
item.description: Nearly three years after the October 7 attacks in Israel, the war in Gaza rages on. Peace activists Aziz Abu Sarah, a Palestinian, and Maoz Inon, an Israeli, joined forces to share their joint message that "the future is peace."

item.title: Hispanic voters moving towards Democrats, CBS News poll shows
item.description: Hispanic and Latino voters are veering towards the Democratic Party, a recent CBS News poll shows. This comes amid rising frustrations over the Trump administration's handling of the economy and harsh immigration policies. The Wall Street Journal national politics reporter, Sabrina Rodriguez, shares her thoughts on the midterm elections.

item.title: "Don't plan on coming to see you": Daughters' statements read as father gets life for wife's murder
item.description: Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole Monday in Ohio after being convicted of murdering his wife, Ashley. At his sentencing, victim impact statements were read from the couple's daughters.

item.title: French high schools closed in biggest day of student protests in decades
item.description: Nationwide protests across France continued for a third week as demonstrators rallied against poor school conditions.

item.title: What we know about the apparent plague death in Russia
item.description: A 28-year-old scientist died in Russia after apparently being exposed to a pneumonic plague strain in a biological laboratory setting. Dr. Amesh Adalja explains more.

item.title: Extended cut: Heroic FlyDubai passengers recall tense moments after pilot was stabbed
item.description: A routine flight became a fight for survival when the co-pilot attacked the captain and tried to crash FlyDubai Flight 1073. As the plane plunged 14,000 feet, people on board helped subdue the attacker while another pilot regained control. Correspondent Matt Gutman sat down with some of the heroes who helped avert disaster.

item.title: Experts and parents discuss consent amid Cornell investigation
item.description: Clinical psychologist Dr. Sheryl Ziegler and educator Jackson Katz join "CBS Mornings" to answer parents' questions about how to talk to their kids about consent in the wake of the investigation into an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house at Cornell University in 2024.

item.title: Make the most of your holiday shopping this year
item.description: Holiday shopping is hitting high gear as Amazon kicks off Prime Big Deal Days. Kelly O'Grady has more.

item.title: Oprah reveals her latest book club pick: "Hungered" by Amanda Rizkalla
item.description: Oprah joins "CBS Mornings" to unveil her 125th book club pick, "Hungered" by Amanda Rizkalla.

item.title: Wisconsin town still waiting for FEMA help after tornado in July
item.description: A Wisconsin community that was ravaged by a tornado in July is still waiting for FEMA aid from the Trump administration. Dr. Jon LaPook reports.

item.title: Nearly 2,000 schools closed in France as students, parents protest
item.description: French students, parents and teachers continued protesting into a third week, saying their schools are falling apart. Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Judge to weigh effort to deport Kilmar Abrego Garcia to Liberia
item.description: The fate of Kilmar Abrego Garcia will again be argued in court on Tuesday when his legal team asks a federal judge to block his deportation to Liberia.

item.title: Jim Bakker, who co-founded "The PTL Club" but fell into disgrace, dies at 86
item.description: Jim Bakker, who along with his first wife Tammy Faye built an evangelical empire around "The PTL Club" TV show, only to lose it all over a sex scandal and financial crimes, has died at 86.

item.title: Rubio calls on Russia to be more open about plague lab worker's death
item.description: The World Health Organization says public risks are low after a plague center worker's death, but Marco Rubio says Moscow should "share more information with the world."

item.title: Coco Gauff decries "insane" amount of online racism after China match dispute
item.description: Coco Gauff said she received an "insane" amount of racist comments on social media following a controversial point in her China Open match against home player Sun Xinran.

item.title: Coca-Cola reveals new flavors for Coke, Powerade and other brands
item.description: Coca-Cola said it will roll out the new flavors, all fruit-inspired, in 2027. Here's what the beverage giant is planning.
